_source: Koolking Industries India Limited DRHP dated 23-Sep-2026 (SEBI filing 01-Oct-2026). Rs crore = Rs million / 10. Page cites are printed DRHP page numbers. Restated standalone financials FY24-FY26 (Ind AS; FY25 and FY24 audited as special-purpose statements); no stub period, no subsidiary. 2:1 bonus (1-Sep-2026) and 1:2 split (3-Sep-2026) are applied to per-share data.

basis.name: Koolking Industries India Limited
basis.outside: merchant-banker section only (named secondary sources, unverified); issuer analysis is from the DRHP

cites.rpt_p: pp. 90-92 (goods and services; excludes Rs 4.99 m freehold land bought from Koolking Foundation in FY26)

1.finding: 2:1 bonus (record date 21-Aug-2026, allotted 1-Sep-2026) and 1:2 split (3-Sep-2026) are applied retrospectively: EPS 6.07 / 4.96 / 1.43 and NAV 17.20 are on 54,729,240 shares. The balance sheet still shows share capital of Rs 91.22 m (pre-bonus count of 9,121,540 shares of Rs 10), which is a presentation point only.

2.finding: Operating cash flow +37.40 / -66.47 / -430.08 Rs m (FY24 / FY25 / FY26) against PAT 76.70 / 271.37 / 332.06; cumulative CFO/PAT -67.5% (-459.15 / 680.13). Operating profit before working capital was positive each year (633.64 in FY26); working capital absorbed Rs 962.71 m in FY26 (inventory Rs 1,017.90 m, receivables Rs 344.94 m, offset by payables Rs 596.42 m). FY26 CFO is also after Rs 74.96 m of foreign-exchange loss in other expenses and Rs 44.24 m of unrealised loss added back.

3.finding: Current tax Rs 107.51 m of a Rs 110.42 m FY26 charge; cumulative current tax is 25.4% of cumulative PBT (236.94 / 933.13 Rs m) against a 25.17% statutory rate. Tax actually paid was Rs 155.57 m over three years, so Rs 92.03 m sits as current tax payable at 31-Mar-2026 (Rs 16.98 m at FY24).

4.finding: Related-party trade is small: purchases from KPM India / KPM International Rs 28.57 m (0.54% of FY26 revenue), sales Rs 2.65 m. Freehold land of Rs 4.99 m was bought from Koolking Foundation (a KMP-influenced entity) in FY26. Promoters lend to the company: unsecured loans of Rs 157.25 m were outstanding at 31-Jul-2026 (8.84% of borrowings, p. 37), and interest paid to promoters, relatives and their HUFs was Rs 13.97 m in FY26. Proceeds go to the company's own plants, not to a subsidiary.

5.finding: Amount-based issue (Rs 3,000 m) with no fixed share count, so no price floor can be set. Specific objects total Rs 2,130.00 m (71.0% of gross proceeds): new units Rs 1,384.73 m, existing-plant machinery Rs 145.27 m, working capital Rs 600.00 m. The balance of Rs 870.00 m must cover offer expenses and general corporate purposes, with GCP capped at 25% of gross proceeds (Rs 750 m); at that cap, offer expenses would be at least Rs 120.00 m.

6.finding: No revaluation reserve in other equity.

7.finding: No goodwill; other intangible assets Rs 0.67 m.

8.finding: Demand side: top-10 customers 89.71% / 89.36% / 88.38% of revenue (FY26 / FY25 / FY24); Amber Enterprises India 28.79%; top-5 customers 75.36%. Supply side: top-10 suppliers 79.33% of expenses; Supplier 1 is 32.99% (22.74% in FY25). Amber Enterprises, the largest customer, is also named among the major suppliers (p. 26); the DRHP does not say how much is bought from it. 53.07% of raw materials are imported (South Korea, China, Thailand). The DRHP states there are no long-term contracts with the top-10 suppliers and purchases are by individual purchase order (p. 430). Both sides fail independently.

9.finding: Contingent liabilities Rs 133.46 m = 14.2% of net worth (Rs 941.17 m) and 30.2% of FY26 PBT; Rs 130.38 m is a customs show-cause notice (22-Apr-2025) on ASEAN-India FTA duty exemption. The High Court dismissed the writ on 28-Apr-2026; a special leave petition (29-May-2026) is pending at the Supreme Court. Not provided for.

R1.finding: Statutory auditor Raj Kumar Jindal & Co resigned 20-Sep-2025 (stated reason: preoccupation with other professional arrangements) after re-appointment on 30-Sep-2024; SCV & Co. LLP was appointed 30-Sep-2025 to fill the vacancy and audited FY26. FY25 and FY24 are special-purpose financial statements. Auditors' reports carry observations on audit trail and on title deeds (p. 59).

R2.finding: CARO / Rule 11(g): audit trail was partly enabled at application level and not at database level throughout FY26. Title deeds of Plot UDL-7 (Gross value Rs 32.22 m, Andhra Pradesh) are not yet in the company's name (held since March 2025; sale deed pending).

R3.finding: Monitoring agency to be appointed (issue above Rs 1,000 m). No debt-repayment object. Land for the three new units is already owned and is not funded from proceeds.

R4.finding: Reg 6(1) re-performed: operating profit 533.77 / 429.41 / 135.94 Rs m reproduces from PBT plus finance cost less other income (442.48 + 117.60 - 26.31 = 533.77); three-year average Rs 366.37 m against the Rs 150 m test; net tangible assets Rs 940.50 / 607.46 / 333.72 m; monetary assets 13.76% / 16.28% / 17.33% of NTA; net worth above Rs 10 m each year. KPI EBITDA Rs 573.88 m reproduces from the P&L.

R5.finding: OFS of 3,050,000 shares by four selling shareholders (915,000 each from three promoters; 305,000 from a promoter-group member), each below half of its holding. At the Rs 115.82 reference the OFS is Rs 353.3 m, 10.5% of a Rs 3353.3 m offer (under the 20% ceiling). Re-test at the RHP price.

R6.finding: Keynote Financial Services is BRLM. This DRHP lists two IPOs handled in FY27: Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (Exports), -23.53% at day 30 and -15.98% at day 90; CSM Technologies, -2.75% at day 30. Neither has a 180-day reading. Both are recorded in data/merchant_bankers.json.

R7.finding: Total project cost of the three new units is Rs 1,530.00 m per the DPR, funded from net proceeds; orders for plant and machinery are yet to be placed (pp. 133-143). Any separate means-of-finance tie-up is not described.

rationale.g1: Revenue Rs 2,399.38 m / 4,831.42 m / 5,267.45 m FY24-FY26: +101.4% then +9.0% (p. 86; MD&A p. 442). The FY26 slowdown came with higher copper and brass prices, so volume growth was lower than 9% (p. 442). The issuer's own working-capital plan takes receivables from Rs 1,061.51 m to Rs 2,200.00 m by FY29 (2.07x, about 27% a year) (pp. 167-168); CARE puts the addressable HVAC-component market at 24.46% CAGR FY26-FY30 and air-conditioner volume at 9.3% (issuer-commissioned, p. 174). Bear (no IPO-funded units) assumes growth below the FY26 rate with the top customers' demand flat; Neutral assumes the new units deliver about 60% of the issuer's plan; Bull assumes growth close to the plan (27% in Y1). The model's opening inputs use FY24 as the base revenue and the FY25-FY26 capex total (Rs 45.13 cr), so growth capex per rupee of added revenue (0.133) is measured over two years: FY26 alone (revenue +9.0%, capex Rs 32.52 cr) would imply 0.65, which is the year of the expansion spend, not of the growth it will bring. IPO capex is placed in Y2 (the issuer schedules it in FY28 and FY29, p. 134).
rationale.m: Reported EBITDA margin 6.52% / 9.50% / 10.89% FY24-FY26; 12.32% adjusted for foreign exchange (pp. 176, 182). FY26 other expenses include a Rs 74.96 m foreign-exchange loss on unhedged imports (p. 444). Gross margin 25.85% / 25.34% / 28.91%. Bear sits below the FY26 reported margin (metal price and FX squeeze); Neutral sits between reported and adjusted (the FX loss recurs in part); Bull is just above the FY26 adjusted margin.
rationale.nwc: Issuer-defined working capital (inventory + receivables + other current assets less payables and other current liabilities) was Rs 242.68 m / 732.56 m / 1,632.48 m = 10.1% / 15.2% / 31.0% of revenue FY24-FY26 (p. 166). Inventory days 51 / 50 / 116; receivable days 86 / 50 / 61 (p. 167). The issuer plans 121 / 107 / 98 inventory days for FY27-FY29 (p. 168). Bear holds the FY26 intensity; Neutral assumes part of the inventory days fall (the plan itself holds about 29% of revenue); Bull assumes the plan's fall to 98 days is fully delivered.
rationale.roic: Issuer-defined adjusted ROCE 23.59% / 43.53% / 32.38% FY24-FY26 (p. 176) on a base that is being tripled by the new units (project cost Rs 1,530.00 m against FY26 net fixed assets of about Rs 0.8 bn, p. 85). No listed peer's ROCE is given; terminal ROIC is set well below the issuer's own figure.
